newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines in mass killing of "Ebola" monkeys.
newsitem.headline: Philippines in mass killing of "Ebola" monkeys.

text.p: Philippine government veterinarians on Tuesday began the mass killing of about 600 monkeys believed infected with the Ebola virus, injecting them with lethal drugs before incinerating them, officials said.

Seven veterinarians took part in the programme in the Ferlite Scientific Research facility in the Laguna province near Manila, the Deparment of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) said in a statement.
"The procedure is an accepted humane method in the veterinary community for the euthanasia of animals," it added.
The department ordered the extermination of the monkeys after several primates believed infected with Ebola died in the facility.
The killings were "in the interest of public health and environmental safety" and to prevent further spread of the deadly virus, it added.
The government quarantined Ferlite last year after two of dozens of monkeys it exported to the United States were found to have been affected by the Ebola Reston virus.
It closed the facility last week after investigation showed the infection continued to circulate in the facility and had spread beyond the cages where the virus was first detected.
The Ebola virus, named after a river in northern Zaire where it was first identified in 1976, causes internal bleeding and an agonising death. Outbreaks in Africa have killed hundreds of people.
The Reston virus was named after a 1989 outbreak wiped out a whole colony of monkeys in a breeding facility in Reston, Virginia.
U.S. and Philippine officials say the strain has not been found to cause illness in humans.

"The DENR shares the sentiments of animal rights activists that this event is indeed unfortunate," the DENR statement said, adding that the procedure it had adopted for killing the monkeys was "to make euthanasia as dignified and as humane as possible."
A DENR official said it was unlikely that all of the monkeys would be killed on Tuesday because of their numbers, and the process would continue "until all of them are killed."
"We have no choice," said the official, asking not to be identified.
